episode.episode: 7-15-26 - Hour 4 - If BYU defeats Notre Dame and Utah will they go 12-0 this season?
episode.showDescription: Cougar Sports with Ben Criddle (@criddlebenjamin) keeps you up-to-date on all things BYU Sports. We not only cover football & basketball, but we dive into recruiting, baseball, soccer, and more. For insight that you can't get anywhere else, tune into 103.9/ 98.3 FM. Monday-Friday from 2-6 PM MST. Follow us on social media @espnthefan & interact with us using #ESPNTheFan.
episode.episodeDescription: Ben Criddle talks BYU sports every weekday from 2 to 6 pm. transcript_window.text: You know, a month ago, we were on the bubble.
I think we were one of the first four teams left out of the tournament, which, you know, that falls short of our expectations at TCU.
You know, being in the DFW Metroplex, so many talented baseball players, such great tradition and history at TCU.
So we fell short of our expectations.
I love our head coach, Kirk Sarlos.
He's done a great job.
We had a pitching coach retire.
We've had some turnover in our staff.
And he's hit the portal fairly hard, which, again, is still kind of counterintuitive to how I was raised in college athletics.
But it's the new reality that we live in.
So really excited about where we're headed.
as we've seen, is just uber competitive in baseball, too.

Schools like West Virginia that used to be an afterthought, Kansas, both nationally hosting regionals, just tells you how attractive this conference is to get athletes not just in football and basketball, but across the board.
In your heyday, what was your pitch combos?
You had a four -pitch option, Arsenal, repertoire, where were you at?
I think Arsenal was being very generous.
Arsenal.
All right, maybe you were more Greg Maddox.
Anything that I have, very daunting.
Well, Tony Gwynn is literally one of the greatest hitters ever to walk the face of.
Like, we were actually having a debate about which swing we would like, and, like, Tony Gwynn came up, like, nine times out of ten, and I was even like, what, Ken Griffey?
No, no, no, Tony Gwynn.
Tony Gwynn was like Mike Tyson in his heyday.
Like, he didn't stand a chance.
No way.
I was a sink or slider guy.
